note: General guidance for the Flathead Valley (USDA Zones 3–5). Timing shifts with elevation and each year's weather; our team is happy to help you plan.

tasks.text: Browse seed catalogs and sketch this year's beds.
Check stored bulbs, tubers and overwintering geraniums for rot or dryness.
Give houseplants your brightest windows and water a little less.
Gently brush heavy snow off evergreen branches before it bends them.

months.name: February
months.summary: The first seeds of the year.

tasks.text: Start onions and slow-growing perennials indoors late in the month.
Prune fruit trees and most deciduous trees while they are dormant.
Set up lights, trays and fresh seed-starting mix.
Plan soil improvements for spring with a soil test.
Start peppers, eggplant and early tomatoes under lights.
Start broccoli, cauliflower and Brussels sprouts for transplanting.
Warm garden soil early with cloches or a cold frame.
Check soil temperatures before sowing anything outdoors.
Sow peas and cool-season greens once the soil can be worked.
Plant asparagus and rhubarb crowns.
Remove winter protection and prune shrub roses as buds swell.
Divide summer- and fall-blooming perennials as they emerge.

months.name: May
months.summary: Planting month, with an eye on frost.

tasks.text: Plant trees and shrubs while spring moisture is on your side.
Harden off seedlings over a week to ten days before planting out.
Plant seed potatoes and onion sets.
Hold tender annuals and tomatoes until frost danger passes, usually late May to early June.
Plant squash, cucumbers and pumpkins once nights stay warm.
Set up drip lines or soaker hoses before the heat arrives.
Feed hanging baskets and containers regularly.
Plant herbs in a sunny spot near the kitchen door.
Water deeply in the morning rather than a little every day.
Snap garlic scapes to send energy to the bulbs.
Watch for aphids and treat early with neem oil.
Pick raspberries and strawberries as they ripen.
Stop fertilizing trees and shrubs so new growth can harden before winter.
Sow a fall crop of lettuce and greens.
Harvest tomatoes and cucumbers often to keep them producing.
Plan where spring bulbs will go this fall.

months.name: September
months.summary: One of the best times to plant.

tasks.text: Plant trees, shrubs and perennials while the soil is still warm.
Plant and divide peonies.
Cover tender crops on frosty nights to stretch the season.
Bring geraniums indoors before the first hard frost.
Plant garlic for next summer's harvest.
Plant tulips, daffodils and other spring bulbs before the ground freezes.
Water trees and evergreens deeply before freeze-up.
Protect roses for winter.
Add fallen leaves to the compost pile.
Wrap young tree trunks against sunscald and rodents.
Mulch perennials once the ground has frozen.
Clean, sharpen and store garden tools.
Move houseplants away from cold drafts and heat vents.
Choose pet-safe houseplants for holiday gifts.
Add houseplants that help freshen indoor air.
Water evergreens during a winter thaw if the ground is dry.
Start a list of vegetables to grow next year.
